reported_use.timing: prophylactic, before the onset of monsoon
reported_use.frequency: one more spray after 45 days; one more if the rainy period is extended
reported_use.other_conditions: for Phytophthora diseases in endemic areas

reported_use.timing: first spray after the pre-monsoon showers
reported_use.frequency: second spray 40-45 days later; a third spray if the monsoon prolongs

chemicals.notes: The institutes recommend this; NutriPalm has NOT verified a product label or registration. Confirm with your agricultural officer or KVK before use.

evidence.quote: It is important to adopt prophylactic treatment in disease endemic areas before the onset of monsoon by spraying 1% Bordeaux mixture and one more spray after 45 days. If the rainy period is extended, one more spray is also required.
evidence.paraphrase: ICAR-CPCRI: before monsoon onset in endemic areas, spray 1% Bordeaux mixture, once more after 45 days, and again if the rains are prolonged.

evidence.quote: Prophylactic spraying with 1 % Bordeaux mixture gives satisfactory control of the disease. Two sprayings are generally required, first after the premonsoon showers and the second 40-45 days thereafter. If the monsoon prolongs, a third spraying will be required.
evidence.paraphrase: CPCRI folder (arecanut Koleroga): 1% Bordeaux mixture prophylactic spraying; two sprays (after pre-monsoon showers and 40-45 days later), a third if the monsoon prolongs.

evidence.quote: Dissolve 1 kg of Copper Sulphate in 50 litres of water
evidence.paraphrase: The folder's preparation instructions begin with dissolving copper sulphate in water.

reported_use.other_conditions: in disease-endemic areas; described as equally effective to the Bordeaux prophylaxis

chemicals.notes: Reported by ICAR-CPCRI as effective against arecanut fruit rot. NutriPalm has NOT verified a registered label for arecanut.

evidence.quote: Spraying of 0.5% mandipropamid 23.4% SC, a contact and translaminar fungicide was found equally effective in managing the fruit rot of arecanut in disease endemic areas.
evidence.paraphrase: Spraying 0.5% mandipropamid 23.4% SC was found equally effective in managing arecanut fruit rot in endemic areas.

chemicals.notes: ICAR-CPCRI names this product for Ganoderma wilt but the passage does not say which crop it applies to, and no label has been verified, so no dose is shown.

evidence.quote: Soil drenching with 1% Bordeaux mixture (40 L/palm) or 0.2% hexaconazole 5EC about 40 L/palm thrice a year for one year or root feeding of hexaconazole 5EC (5 mL per 100 mL of water) at quarterly intervals till complete recovery of the palm.
evidence.paraphrase: The article lists soil drenching or root feeding for Ganoderma wilt without stating the crop for each treatment.
